Join the Las Virgenes Creek Cleanup Senior Center to Host Country Western BBQ Know Your Rights Seminar for Businesses June 12, 2025 Father’s Day Concert Kicks Off Summer Concerts in the Park Season Valley Cultural Foundation is excited to announce a special Father’s Day Concert at Warner Park on Sunday, June 15! This family-friendly evening will kick off VCF’s 50th anniversary summer season with live music, local food, and interactive fun for all ages. Don’t miss this chance to celebrate Dad with great entertainment and community spirit under the stars. Each concert begins at 5:30 pm with an Emerging Artist Showcase, spotlighting fresh, original talent. On June 15, that spotlight shines on Eye of the Sun, an exciting new voice in alternative rock. Then, at 6:30 pm, get ready for No Duh, the nation’s top tribute to Gwen Stefani and No Doubt, delivering a high-energy show packed with fan favorites. In addition to the music, concertgoers can explore local vendors, indulge in food trucks, and enjoy a festive atmosphere that’s made this series a cherished Valley tradition. A special Kids Zone, featuring interactive exhibits from the Discovery Cube, creative activities, and fun hosted by the YMCA, ensures that even the youngest guests have a day to remember. Bring your fathers and join in the fun for a special celebration day at the park! Grab your blankets, rally your friends and family, and come early to snag the best spot. The summer vibes are calling - and VCF’s 50th anniversary kick-off celebration is one you won’t want to miss. All concerts take place in Warner Park, Topanga Canyon Blvd. at Califa Street in Woodland Hills. For a full schedule visit valleycultural.org. No Duh will kick off the concert season June 15. Join the Calabasas Chamber’s Birthday Celebration Join the Calabasas Chamber for a special community-wide birthday party on Friday, June 27, from 6 to 10 pm at the Calabasas Country Club. The 70th anniversary celebration is presented by the Calabasas Chamber of Commerce and sponsored by Poppy Bank. Long-time members, former chamber members, local businesses, and the Calabasas community are invited to join the evening of reflection, networking, and celebration. Guests will have the opportunity to indulge in a BBQ buffet, cake, dancing, history display, presentations, raffles, and more! DJ Spotlight LA will curate the party music for the evening. The chamber will also be honoring the following 30-year Milestone Members for their dedication and contributions to the chamber and the Calabasas community: The Acorn; James R. Bozajian; Executive-Suite Services; Inc., Gelson’s Markets; and Las Virgenes Municipal Water District. Visit calabasaschamber.com to learn more about the 70-year history of the Calabasas Chamber and upcoming events and purchase tickets for the anniversary celebration.
Valley News Group June 12, 2025 Page 9 HEALTH & BEAUTY Learn Pickleball Precision at Q4: Mastering the Overhead & Dinking Game Take your pickleball game to the next level with a focused workshop at Q4 Active on two of the sport’s most critical - and injury-prone - skills: the overhead and the dink. You’ll learn how to safely and powerfully perform overhead shots with proper form and shoulder mechanics, while also improving your finesse and control at the net. The workshop will be held Saturday, June 14, at 1:15 pm. Q4 Active is located at 6200 Variel Avenue, Suite 2A, Woodland Hills. RSVP at q4-active.com or by calling (818) 961-5353. Assemblymember Jesse Gabriel, center, with from left, Saif Mogri, Adnan Hamid, Project Rise Community Outreach Leaders; Aamir Turab Hatami, Nominee of Dawat Hadiyah America, and Sakina Diwan, Project Rise Community Outreach Coordinator. Assemblymember Gabriel Names Project Rise as His 2025 Nonprofit of the Year Assemblymember Jesse Gabriel (D - Encino) honored Project Rise, a Dawoodi Bohra Initiative, as his 2025 California Nonprofit of the Year for Assembly District 46. Assemblymember Gabriel was accompanied by (from left to right) Sakina Diwan, Project Rise Community Outreach Coordinator, Saif Mogri, Aamir Turab Hatami, Nominee of Dawat Hadiyah America, and Adnan Hamid, Project Rise Community Outreach Leader, for a luncheon in the State’s Capitol, where they received the honor and recognition. Launched in June 2018, Project Rise is a philanthropic initiative committed to addressing the needs of marginalized communities through a variety of impactful programs. With a core focus on tackling issues like malnutrition and environmental conservation, the organization has made significant strides in both global and local efforts, demonstrating unwavering dedication to environmental sustainability, humanitarian service, and interfaith collaboration. “Project Rise has been an incredibly dedicated partner in protecting the environment, promoting interfaith collaboration, and serving the most vulnerable in our community,” said Assemblymember Jesse Gabriel (D-Encino). “I’m so grateful for their service and I am proud to recognize them as our 2025 Nonprofit of the Year.” “We are honored and grateful to Assemblymember Jesse Gabriel for nominating Project Rise – A Dawoodi Bohra Initiative – as a 2025 Nonprofit of the Year,” said Aamir Hatimi, representing The Dawoodi Bohras of Los Angeles. “This recognition reaffirms our commitment to uplifting communities and addressing global development challenges, ranging from hunger and poverty to climate crisis and education through compassion, sustainability, and service. We share this honor with many dedicated volunteers and partners who make our mission possible every day.” Project Rise is an active community partner in the West San Fernando Valley. For each of the last three years, Project Rise has participated in Assemblymember Gabriel’s Annual Valley Day of Service, sponsoring thousands of lunch kits that are distributed to local food pantries and homelessness outreach organizations. Project Rise also took the lead on multiple efforts to support fire relief efforts following the Palisades and AltadVV6ena fires, donating outreach kits for the City of Los Angeles’ Inside Safe program, and coordinating community cleanups with Volunteers Cleaning Communities. Valley News Group June 12, 2025 Page 11 REAL ESTATE Summit to Summit Hike in Calabasas Saturday The City of Calabasas is leading a hike this Saturday, June 14, on the Summit to Summit Motorway. Meet at 7:30 am at 3314 Adamsville Avenue for the Bill Would Add 118,000 Acres to Santa Monica Mountains Recreation Area U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) and U.S. Representative Laura Friedman (D-Calif.-30) introduced the bicameral reintroduction of the Rim of the Valley Corridor Preservation Act, landmark legislation that would protect some of the last wild and open spaces in the Los Angeles area and allow the National Park Service to work with local communities to better protect natural resources and improve access to nature. This bill would add over 118,000 acres to the Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area (SMMNRA) and is based on a National Park Service study that was reported to Congress in 2016. The Rim of the Valley stretches from the Simi Hills and Santa Susanas to the Verdugos and the San Gabriel Mountains, making a “green belt” that encircles the San Fernando, La Crescenta, Santa Clarita, Simi, and Conejo Valleys. “The Rim of the Valley contains some of the last wild and open spaces in Los Angeles and connects our urban city centers and suburbs with the beautiful outdoors. This legislation will preserve the land and wildlife that millions of Angelenos enjoy. We must protect these natural treasures for future generations, so they too can experience the beautiful hiking, abundant wildlife, diverse ecosystem, and significant historic sites found in the Santa Monica Mountains Recreation Area,” said Senator Schiff. “The Rim of the Valley is one of Southern California’s most important natural treasures. We must protect these lands so that every Californian and American can enjoy them for generations to come,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman (D-Calif.-30). “Not only will this legislation provide local communities with better access to our beautiful public lands, but it will ensure that we protect the natural resources and wildlife that call the Rim of the Valley home.” The bill has been endorsed by Active San Gabriel Valley, Amigos de los Rios, Audubon Center at Debs Park, Chinese Historical Society of Southern California, Citizens for Los Angeles Wildlife, Community Hiking Club, City of Santa Clarita, Friends of Grifith Park, Los Angeles Equine Advisory Committee, National Parks Conservation Association, Nature For All, Outward Bound Adventures, Poison Free Malibu, Santa Susana Mountain Park Association, St. Francis Dam Memorial Foundation, Bolsa Chica Land Trust, Central Valley Partnership, Endangered Habitats League, Environmental Center of San Diego, Environmental Protection Information Center (EPIC), Friends of Whittier Hills, Los Padres ForestWatch, Mendocino Producers Guild, Outdoor Alliance, Resource Renewal Institute, The River Project, Friends of the Inyo, Klamath Forest Alliance, and California Native Plant Society.
